violations.explanation: The previous-page IconButton has no tooltip and its Icon has no semanticLabel, so screen readers announce only 'button' with no indication of its purpose.
The next-page IconButton has no tooltip and its Icon has no semanticLabel, so assistive technologies cannot convey its purpose.

violations.affected_code: onPressed: () async { if (_currentPage >= 1) {...} }, icon: _currentPage == 0 ? const Icon(Icons.arrow_back, color: Colors.white38) : ...
violations.explanation: On the first page the button is only visually dimmed, but onPressed is still non-null. Screen readers therefore announce it as enabled even though it does nothing. Set onPressed to null when navigation is unavailable so the disabled state is exposed.

violations.affected_code: onPressed: () async { if (_currentPage < widget.totalPages - 1) {...} }, icon: _currentPage == widget.totalPages - 1 ? const Icon(Icons.arrow_forward, color: Colors.white38) : ...
violations.explanation: On the last page the next button looks disabled but is still semantically enabled, because onPressed is non-null. This misleads assistive technology users.

violations.type: Missing live region / state change announcement
violations.explanation: The page indicator updates when pages change, but it is not wrapped in Semantics(liveRegion: true). Screen reader users are therefore not informed of the new page position after activating the buttons.
